text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Lyonnaise des Eaux posts a 1.35 billion franc profit for 1996. Generale des Eaux returns to profit, posting a 1.95 billion franc profit for 1996.
-- Pharmaceutical laboratories Bio-Merieux and Oris consider a merger.
-- Eurotunnel expects to resume lorry traffic in the Channel tunnel on June 15, after a November 1996 fire.
-- Canal Plus may join with Time Warner to bid for cable-TV operator Compagnie Generale de Videocommunication.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Banking workers to strike today against planned reform of a 1937 banking sector decree on branch opening hours.
-- EU Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy rules out delaying implementation of a single European currency.
-- U.S. clothing company BCBG to bid for ailing children's clothing chain Jacadi, seeks to grow in Europe.
-- Court to rule today on complaint filed by association of minority shareholders of Comipar-Banque Pallas Stern over false accounts and misleading information for years 1992 and 1993.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Government will reject Britain's GEC as a candidate to acquire the state's 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF on Monday.
-- Brussels labour court rules Renault violate labour rules in announcing shutdown of Vilvoorde, Belgium.
-- TF1 chairman Patrick Le Lay says in an interview he expects TPS to become a leader in digital TV.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer says may close Vilvoorde plant before July 31 if its workers do not resume production.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Lyonnaise des Eaux and Generale des Eaux both expect strong 1997 profits.
